Memory limit delegates engine; custom allocator caveat. Stack limit zero or >16MiB disables check; policy must validate limits before setter.
Interrupt polling occurs when counter expires; calls registered callback, throws interruption. No arbitrary parser/builtin/host-call preemption guarantee follows.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Trusted source compilation and denied dynamic compilation share engine machinery
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Deleting global Function/eval leaves constructors reachable through prototypes or host callables; omitting Eval also breaks source compilation. Constructor-generated code skips AST instrumentation.
minimum_controls: Explicit trusted compiler/evaluator boundary and engine-level disabled eval_internal in execution realm, or separately inspected complete equivalent denial; never rely on source token blacklist/global deletion.
Prove constructor chains of ordinary functions, host callbacks, computed keys, Reflect/prototype routes and generator/async intrinsics; only allowlisted syntax enters trusted instrumenting compiler.
future_acceptance: Independent dynamic-code bypass corpus; compile ordinary expressions successfully while every denied path fails with preserved original text and source diagnostics.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Checkpoint budgets do not bound arbitrary engine/host work
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: A single builtin, expensive getter, conversion, huge string or blocking host callback consumes work without another AST loop checkpoint; Pending retries amplify work.
minimum_controls: Separate deterministic shared semantic fuel from nondeterministic safety deadline; charge parse/rewrite/compile, nested reads/retries, callbacks, result extraction/getters and host copies.
Worker-level enforced containment and bounded retirement; no exact interrupt/deadline guarantee for arbitrary C/host calls.
future_acceptance: Long builtin/parser and hanging-hostcall negative cases; timeout outcome cannot promote partial result; independent worker liveness/resource oracle.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Bytecode cache is a trusted executable artifact boundary
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Imported/tampered cache has matching engine version or checksum but bypasses profile and AST checks; checksum escape accepted by engine does not authenticate artifacts.
minimum_controls: Only trusted compiler-produced bytecode; never deserialize document/vendor-supplied bytecode.

Cache key binds original/canonical source, AST transform/instrumentation/source-map versions, engine C source/wrapper/build features/ABI/target/endianness, profile/host API semantics; integrity verified before unsafe load; compile source on mismatch.
Do not share runtime-bound function/value handles across runtimes; cache artifacts contain no live content/grants.
future_acceptance: Tamper, engine-feature/profile change, wrong target and absent provenance reject before load; cache hit/miss yields equivalent budgeted semantics.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Thread synchronization and memory setters are not complete worker bounds
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: A setting greater than16MiB disables stack checks; another dependency enables allocator feature; callback reenters locked runtime or one shared runtime stalls every property.
minimum_controls: Validate stack0<limit<=16MiB and nonzero heap before execution; lockfile/feature closure verifies no custom allocator unless independently quota-proved.
Owned dedicated worker/runtime with no host lock across callback reentry; cancel signal does not wait for runtime lock.
Aggregate runtime/realm/compile/cache/snapshot/result/retiring-byte admission under existing owners, held until actual reclamation.
future_acceptance: Feature-unification and bad-limit cases fail closed; callback reentry/saturation/cancel cases do not deadlock; measured aggregate host RSS includes retired realms and compilation.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Deterministic profile requires closed reachable intrinsics
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Fresh realm still has engine Date/Math.random/locale behavior or mutable prototypes; host object conversion invokes nondeterministic methods.
minimum_controls: Allowlisted intrinsics; deterministic Date/locale/random wrappers must cover prototype/constructor routes and use immutable canonical revision/tick/seed identity.
Disable async/job/module/shared-memory/native access at engine plus syntax boundary; wrappers and host data are read-only and namespace-protected; unsupported source preserved.
Version numeric/transcendental/nonfinite semantics and platform tolerance or exactness; never claim ES2018 shape proves full Adobe compatibility.
future_acceptance: Changed OS locale/timezone/time and render order, layer reorder, prototype mutation and constructor routes; compare exact tick/property values and independent reference pixels.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Source rewrite and replay must preserve semantics and exact identities
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Compound indexed assignment with side-effecting getter evaluates reference twice; integer IDs above2^53 collide; replay or layer reorder changes random results.
minimum_controls: Real binding-aware AST lowering and source maps preserve evaluation order/coercion; stable opaque IDs and canonical tick, no f64 identity or layer-index seed.
Dependency graph commit checks plus guarded dynamic activation; nested replay consumes same budget; pure immutable host reads.
future_acceptance: Side-effecting accessors/computed references and alias shadowing corpus; >2^53 identity distinction; cycle/replay/reorder deterministic independent oracle.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Detachment must reject oversized and active outputs
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Result array silently truncates or accessor runs unbounded work while converting out of VM; Rust buffers exceed heap cap.
minimum_controls: Strict bounded inert result schema; invalid/oversize returns typed error instead of truncation.
Budget depth/entries/bytes before copies; reject accessors/proxies or instrument and debit any permitted extraction work; host result allocation counted separately.
future_acceptance: Oversized/deep/cyclic/proxy/getter outputs fail explicitly with no accepted partial result or leaked buffer.

INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.title: Motion remains engine-neutral and JS provider optional
INDEPENDENT_FINDINGS.counterexample: Motion core links rquickjs/QuickJS C or exposes Context/JsValue types; missing JS engine disables unrelated keyframe/render foundations or causes silent Boa fallback.
minimum_controls: Neutral typed Motion expression port; separate optional JS provider closure with failunsupported; no engine-native types/second store/scheduler leak.
All executable module foundations before features; provider source pin/version and independently proved host support, no automatic alternate engine fallback.
Reuse Effect semantic fixtures selectively, not Boa production isolation/runtime/cache ownership.
future_acceptance: Base Motion build closure independent of JS/native C; optional provider absent returns explicit diagnostics while core capabilities execute; actual Handshake embedding distinct portability proof.

decision_review.observed: Actual draft includes explicit dynamic-compiler restriction, result conversion, ownership/reclamation, bounded aggregate resources and neutral optional JS provider. Own Rust preference correctly refers to domain/AST/profile implementation; Boa remains conditional candidate.

corrections.text: The production JavaScript AST/parser/lowering/checkpoint-instrumentation owner is NOT_ESTABLISHED by rquickjs or Effect source. Name and implement that owner as an executable prerequisite; ordinary engine interrupt polls are not semantic AST fuel. Instrument every admitted control-flow and function/callback entry, preserve evaluation order and source maps, and charge nested reads, retries and result conversion to the same immutable job allowance. Activation fails when a syntax path lacks proved instrumentation.
corrections.reason: Existing language runtime and Rust preference do not establish a usable engine-neutral AST/fuel implementation; plan must make this connected predecessor explicit.

corrections.text: Cached executable identity MUST include canonical source digest, parser/AST-lowering/checkpoint/source-map versions, deterministic profile and host API semantics, exact wrapper plus bundled C/build-feature/patch/target/endianness identity. Only trusted compiler-produced artifacts may enter unsafe bytecode decode; matching engine format version/checksum alone is insufficient. Cache mismatch recompiles preserved source or fails unavailable, never adopts supplied executable bytes.
corrections.reason: Engine/profile/ABI/schema identity currently broad; explicitly bind trusted semantic transform and instrumentation inputs to avoid stale uninstrumented cached code.
